children: A number of stocks fell in the afternoon session after AI linked stocks continued to pull back as Anthropic slid nearly 14% following its debut, failing to revive confidence in the sector's spending boom.

Investors had looked to Anthropic's record $81.3 billion initial public offering and Nvidia's quarterly earnings beat under interim CEO Colette Kress to steady sentiment following Jensen Huang's resignation, CNBC reported. Instead, Anthropic's retreat toward its $83 offer price echoed Seaport Research warnings, covered by CNBC, that its valuation demands much faster revenue growth.

Separately, Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook warned against delaying rate hikes ahead of an expected December increase. Compounding the concerns, President Donald Trump threatened penalties on overseas U.S. data-center builds as new Commerce Department export-licensing rules weighed on chipmakers.
The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks.
Among others, the following stocks were impacted:
Hardware & infrastructure company Cipher Digital fell 16.6%.
Hardware & infrastructure company Kingsoft Cloud Holdings fell 7%.
Hardware & infrastructure company Keel Infrastructure fell 17.5%.
Hardware & infrastructure company Nebius Group fell 14.3%.
Hardware & infrastructure company D-Wave Quantum fell 9.9%.

Keel Infrastructure’s shares are extremely volatile and have had 103 moves greater than 5% over the last year. But moves this big are rare even for Keel Infrastructure and indicate this news significantly impacted the market’s perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was 4 days ago when the stock dropped 7% on the news that the Commerce Department moved to shut down a loophole letting Chinese companies lease Nvidia computing power overseas, intensifying concern that Nvidia’s leadership upheaval could curb its financing of server and cloud buildouts ahead of third-quarter earnings later in the week, CNBC reported. Goldman Sachs analyst James Schneider warned in a client note cited by CNBC that new multi-party ecosystem deals may prove harder to negotiate.

Server builders and debt-financed neoclouds rely on uninterrupted GPU allocations, accessible credit, and broad end-user demand to convert backlogs into cash flow. As a result, restricting third-country compute leasing could narrow overseas capacity demand.

Keel Infrastructure is down 45.6% since the beginning of the year, and at $1.42 per share, it is trading 78.8% below its 52-week high of $6.66 from June 2026. Investors who bought $1,000 worth of Keel Infrastructure’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at only $190.19.
